title: The Eye of the Sahara

beats.text: Type these coordinates into a satellite map, and you'll find something strange in the middle of the Sahara.
A giant eye, forty kilometers wide. Astronauts use it as a landmark from space.
Some people say this is the lost city of Atlantis.
But the truth is way older. About a hundred million years ago, molten rock pushed the ground up into a giant dome.
Then wind and rain wore it down, layer by layer, until only these rings were left.
The Eye of the Sahara isn't a lost city. It's the inside of an ancient dome, laid open by the wind.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: The Richat Structure in Mauritania, the Eye of the Sahara, is about 40 km wide and a landmark for astronauts. Some claim it is Atlantis. Geologists say it is a deeply eroded dome pushed up by magma about 100 million years ago. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: NASA (ISS030-E-12516, public domain); Clemens Schmillen, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.
